clause.quote: Given a local or remote event, a non-controller, non-witness, non-delegator validator MUST first verify the event's controller signatures, witness signatures (if witnessed), and delegator anchoring seal (if delegated) before it can accept that event into its copy of that event's KEL.

inferred_from.inference: The sentence states what a validator must verify before it can accept an event, not that it must accept one that passes. No sentence obliges a validator to accept anything, so that a validator should accept an event that passes every check, and that the event is then on the trunk, is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, KERI, What MUST means here).

clause.quote: In order to verify signatures, a verifier MUST first determine which set of keys are or were the controlling set for the AID of that event when the event was issued.

A [[ref: Validator]] that receives a key event or non-key-event message that does not have attached at least one verifiable Controller signature MUST drop that message (i.e., not escrow or otherwise accept it).

spec_conflicts.quote: A Validator MAY drop any provided key event message body that does not have at least one attached signature from the current controlling key state of the AID of the associated [[ref: KEL]].
spec_conflicts.why: Line 541 makes dropping an unsigned key event a MAY; line 1266 makes it a MUST. The cases follow line 1266, the later and more specific sentence.

description: An inception, then an interaction at sequence number 2 whose signature was not made by the current key, then the interaction at 1. The early event cannot be verified when it arrives, but once its prior is accepted the validator holds the key it should have been signed with. It must never accept it.
title: Early event with a forged signature
